_comment: The 'Mangal' — a tank wearing a welded shed. Authored from reference photographs at
incoming/factions/russian-federation/units/mangal/ (gitignored: third-party rights, and
they inform PARAMETERS only — silhouette, proportion, palette — never pixels).
SECOND PASS, after seeing it in game and against a better reference frame. Three things
the first pass got wrong, all of them shape rather than detail:
1. IT IS WIDE. The shed is nearly as wide as it is tall and only about 1.5x longer than
wide — a squat box, not the long narrow wedge the side-on still suggested.
2. THE ROOF IS FLAT, or very nearly. The sides are VERTICAL and the top is a shallow
pitch of corrugated sheet. The first pass read the side profile as a triangular prism
and set ridgeWidth 0.18, which is a tent; the truth is a box with a lid on it, so the
ridge is now a separate shallow part at ridgeWidth 0.78.
3. THERE IS A TURRET. It traverses only a little, but it exists and it is visible
through the open front. The first pass asserted the carapace was welded solid and
that there was deliberately no TURRET sub-object — that was wrong, and it was wrong
in the direction of making a limitation sound like a design decision.
THIRD PASS, one correction and it is again the SILHOUETTE rather than any detail: the
shed is built AROUND the tank, not perched on top of it. Its walls come down past the
hull and hang over the tracks to about their mid-height — which is the whole visual
idea of the thing, an armoured box with a vehicle somewhere inside it. Two passes had
the carapace floor at z = 13.5, clear of tracks that stop at z = 9, so the tank read as
a shed sitting on a chassis with daylight between them.
The wall is now 36 wide against tracks 34 across their outer faces. That one unit of
overhang per side is not styling: coplanar faces Z-FIGHT, and a skirt flush with the
track it covers flickers between the two surfaces as the camera moves.
+X is FORWARD, matching how retail vehicles are laid out. Z is up, z = 0 is the ground,
so a part's `at` is the CENTRE of its box.
STILL DELIBERATELY NOT GEOMETRY: the cope-cage grid, the camo netting, and the road
wheels. All three are wire, mesh or repetition — texture work at a 245-triangle peer
budget. The wheels cost 55% of the first pass's triangles and were invisible inside the
track boxes; retail reaches the same conclusion, carrying flat tread strips with the links
painted on.
name: MANGAL

mangal.tga._: Weathered olive drab for the hull and the shed's flanks. `ao` and `lip` are the
mangal.tga.__: two that matter: a retail 256x256 vehicle sheet is not more colourful than ours
mangal.tga.___: and not higher frequency — it has dark occlusion in every recess and a bright lip
mangal.tga.____: on every top edge, and that is what makes a flat polygon read as a panelled one.

mangal_roof.tga._: Corrugated rust sheet. Narrow panels at strong occlusion IS corrugation once it is
mangal_roof.tga.__: texture rather than geometry — the ribs are the shadow between the sheets.

mangal_tread.tga._: THE ONE SHEET THAT IS NOT A REGION OF THE ATLAS, because a scrolling tread cannot
mangal_tread.tga.__: be. W3DTankDraw animates a belt by adding to the mesh's U offset, so UVs confined
mangal_tread.tga.___: to a sub-rectangle would scroll straight out of it and into the hull's. Retail says
mangal_tread.tga.____: the same by construction: NVGattTank's body is on NVGattTank.tga and its two treads
mangal_tread.tga.______: 128 rather than 256 because it is one belt seen edge-on, and it must TILE — the
mangal_tread.tga._______: wrap crosses the screen several times a second once the thing is moving.
mangal_tread.tga.________: NO ROAD WHEELS, and that reverses what the atlas pass concluded. Painting the
mangal_tread.tga._________: wheels was right while the belt was STATIC — they were invisible geometry inside
mangal_tread.tga.__________: the track box and cost 55% of the model's triangles. A W3DTankDraw belt animates
mangal_tread.tga.___________: by sliding the whole sheet along U, so a painted wheel travels down the hull with
mangal_tread.tga.____________: the links. A link is the only thing on a real track that moves; it is the only
mangal_tread.tga.______________: Darker than the hull's olive on purpose. This sheet is the one surface
mangal_tread.tga._______________: the AO bake does not reach — it left the atlas — so it has to carry its
mangal_tread.tga.________________: own tone, or a belt tucked under an overhanging carapace renders as the
mangal_tread.tga._______________: COARSE ON PURPOSE. At uvScale 16 this sheet repeats three times
mangal_tread.tga.________________: along the 48-long run and a pitch of 32 gives four links per
mangal_tread.tga._________________: repeat — twelve links on the vehicle, each four world units. The
mangal_tread.tga.__________________: earlier thirty-two were a fine hatch: correct as a surface, and
mangal_tread.tga.___________________: impossible to tell apart from a stationary one when it scrolled.
mangal_tread.tga.____________________: A moving texture has to be legible at the speed it moves.

mangal_house.tga._: The house-colour plate, and it is painted NEARLY WHITE on purpose. Recolouring SETS
mangal_house.tga.__: the vertex material's ambient and diffuse to the team colour — the engine's own
mangal_house.tga.___: comment says it ignores whatever was there and assumes 1.0 — and the texture still
mangal_house.tga.____: modulates. So the pixel is texture x teamColour: a light plate reads as the team's
mangal_house.tga._____: actual colour, and an olive one would read as muddy olive for every player alike.
mangal_house.tga.______: hatches and grilles are switched OFF explicitly, because an atlas region
mangal_house.tga._______: inherits them from the sheet's base spec — the first render put a big dark
mangal_house.tga.________: access hatch in the middle of the team-colour plate.

parts._: Track runs. Links and road wheels are painted, not modelled — see the note above.
parts.___: TWO PARTS NOW, NOT ONE MIRRORED PART, and the names are the reason. W3DTankDraw
parts.____: finds a belt by _strnicmp(meshName, "TREADS", 6) and reads the SEVENTH character
parts._____: for the side, scrolling L forwards and R backwards. A single mirrored mesh has one
parts.______: name and can only be one side, so the mirror had to go. +Y is to the LEFT with +X
parts._______: forward and Z up, which is what puts TREADSL at y = +13.5.
parts.name: TREADSL

parts._: The right belt. Authored rather than mirrored, for the naming reason above.
parts.name: TREADSR

parts._: The hull under the shed. Visible through the open front and whenever the camera
parts.__: drops, so it cannot be omitted however well the carapace hides it from above.
parts.name: HULL

parts._: THE CARAPACE — a box with VERTICAL sides, not a prism, and it goes DOWN. It spans
parts.__: z 4.5 to 26.5: from the middle of the track runs to the eaves, so the hull and the
parts.___: inner half of each track are inside it and the outer half is behind a skirt. That
parts.____: is what 'a tank wearing a welded shed' has to look like from the side — two passes
parts._____: left its floor at 13.5, above tracks that stop at 9, and the daylight between them
parts.________: The front is cut clean through so the turret inside is visible, which is the one
parts._________: feature a texture genuinely cannot fake: the silhouette has to have a hole in it.
parts.__________: Cut coordinates are LOCAL to the part, so the cut's z tracks the part's centre —
parts.___________: it moved with the box rather than staying where it was.
parts.name: CARAPACE

parts._: The lid, and it now CAPS A TAPER rather than sitting on a vertical box. The video
parts.__: reference settles an argument the first two passes both got wrong in opposite
parts.___: directions: the shed is neither a tent (pass one, ridgeWidth 0.18) nor a flat-
parts.____: sided crate (pass two). It is a truncated pyramid — big flat panels sloping down
parts._____: and OUTWARD from a narrow ridge to a skirt wider than the tracks, which is what
parts.______: makes the front view a trapezoid. The slope is the CARAPACE's taper; this part is
parts._______: only the shallow peak sitting on its narrow top (27 x 21 after tapering).
parts.name: ROOF

parts._: THE CASEMATE, and the name is the decision. It was called TURRET, and that name is
parts.__: read: `zhasset artprofile` declares a turret when a part is called exactly TURRET,
parts.___: and the compiler then emits both an AIUpdateInterface Turret block and a
parts.____: `Turret = TURRET` draw line off the back of it.
parts.______: ZH HAS NO TURRET ARC. TurretAIData::buildFieldParse carries eighteen keys and not
parts._______: one bounds azimuth — MinIdleScanAngle/MaxIdleScanAngle limit the idle wander only,
parts.________: TurretFireAngleSweep is a sweep while firing, and the weapon's MinTargetPitch /
parts._________: MaxTargetPitch are elevation. A gun is 360 degrees or it is fixed. So a vehicle
parts.__________: whose gun is welded inside a box of armour has to be FIXED, and the piece of
parts.___________: geometry behind the opening must not be called TURRET — a part named for a thing
parts.____________: it cannot do is a lie in the exact place four different tools go looking.
parts.name: CASEMATE

parts._: THE HOUSE-COLOUR PLATE — the cheapest thing on this model and the one that says
parts.__: whose unit it is. Two quads' worth of geometry per flank, and the engine finds it
parts.___: the same way it finds a tread: by the mesh NAME. _strnicmp(meshName, "HOUSECOLOR",
parts.____: 10) makes the whole submesh's vertex material take the player's colour, which is
parts._____: why this is a separate part rather than a painted stripe on the carapace — a
parts.______: material is per-mesh, so a stripe can only be recoloured by being its own mesh.
parts._______: Mirrored, because both flanks carry one and neither name is load-bearing per side.
parts.name: HOUSECOLOR01
parts._x: The wall SLOPES now, so a flat plate's standoff is a function of its height: the
parts._y: half-width runs 18 at the skirt to 10.4 at the ridge. At z = 13 the wall is at
parts._z: 15.1, and a 1.4-thick plate centred on 15.4 sits roughly flush across its own
parts._w: 3.6 of rise. Left at the old y = 18.3 it floated five units clear in mid-air.

parts._: Gun, out of the turret and through the opening.
parts.name: BARREL

_bones: Pivots with no geometry, which is how a model tells the engine things it cannot see.
TREADFX01 and TREADFX02 are read by computeTrackSpacing: it measures the distance between
them and adds one belt width (4.0) to get how wide the mud ribbon should be. Missing, it
falls back to a fixed default sized for nothing in particular. Placed at the REAR of each
belt at ground level, matching NVGattTank's own four TREADFX pivots.
03 and 04 are the front pair. Nothing reads them today — the engine takes 01 and 02 only —
but retail carries all four and they cost 60 bytes each.

track_rf.tga._: The mud, laid on the terrain rather than on the tank — so no mesh names it and it
track_rf.tga.__: is declared here instead of under `textures`. 32-bit: the terrain-track shader is
track_rf.tga.___: _PresetAlphaShader and the alpha channel IS the mark.
